message:
## Vulnerability Digest

This primary product scan combined and deduplicated entries from `Products.txt` and `List_of_SIA_Completed.txt` only. `DLL_software_component.txt` was not read or combined. The scan window was **2026-10-13 23:40 UTC through 2026-10-14 23:40 UTC** (**2026-10-14 05:10 IST through 2026-10-15 05:10 IST**).

New, credible findings were confirmed for Windows, Microsoft .NET Framework, NGINX, OpenSSH, and Ubuntu packages. The Windows Shell issue is actively exploited and warrants immediate review.

### Finding 1 — Windows Shell security-feature bypass

- **Product:** Windows 10 / Windows Server 2012 R2
- **Issue:** CVE-2026-96951
- **Severity:** High, CVSS 8.8
- **Description:** Command injection in Windows Shell can let an unauthenticated remote attacker convince a user to open a crafted file, bypass Mark of the Web protections, and potentially execute commands.
- **Relevance:** Windows 10 and Windows Server 2012 R2 are both in the monitored product scope; Microsoft and national cyber authorities report exploitation in the wild.
- **Sources:** [CVE record](https://www.cve.org/CVERecord?id=CVE-2026-96951), [CERT-In advisory](https://www.cert-in.org.in/s2cMainServlet?VLCODE=CIAD-2026-0047&pageid=PUBVLNOTES02), [NHS England Cyber Alert](https://digital.nhs.uk/cyber-alerts/2026/cc-4867)

### Finding 2 — .NET Framework security-feature bypass

- **Product:** Microsoft .NET Framework
- **Issue:** CVE-2026-108398
- **Severity:** High, CVSS 8.8
- **Description:** An untrusted search-path flaw can allow a low-privileged local attacker to make .NET Framework resolve an attacker-controlled file and bypass a security boundary.
- **Relevance:** Microsoft .NET and multiple .NET Framework versions are explicitly present in the monitored lists. The issue was publicly disclosed with Microsoft’s October updates.
- **Source:** [NHS England Cyber Alert](https://digital.nhs.uk/cyber-alerts/2026/cc-4867)

### Finding 3 — NGINX buffer overflow with alias and rewrite

- **Product:** NGINX
- **Issue:** CVE-2026-15176
- **Severity:** Medium (NGINX rating)
- **Description:** Specific `alias`, `rewrite`, and `$request_filename` configurations can trigger a heap buffer overflow from crafted HTTP requests.
- **Relevance:** Direct match to the monitored NGINX product.
- **Affected versions:** 0.1.29 through 1.31.6; fixed in 1.30.6 and 1.31.7.
- **Source:** [NGINX security advisories](https://nginx.org/en/security_advisories.html)

### Finding 4 — NGINX script-evaluation buffer overflow

- **Product:** NGINX
- **Issue:** CVE-2026-93479
- **Severity:** Medium (NGINX rating)
- **Description:** Evaluation of string expressions containing variables can cause a buffer overflow.
- **Relevance:** Direct match to the monitored NGINX product.
- **Affected versions:** 1.30.0–1.30.5 and 1.31.2–1.31.6; fixed in 1.30.6 and 1.31.7.
- **Source:** [NGINX security advisories](https://nginx.org/en/security_advisories.html)

### Finding 5 — NGINX HTTP/3 request-body injection

- **Product:** NGINX
- **Issue:** CVE-2026-95101
- **Severity:** Medium (NGINX rating)
- **Description:** A flaw in HTTP/3 request-body handling can allow request-body injection in affected configurations.
- **Relevance:** Direct match to the monitored NGINX product.
- **Affected versions:** 1.25.0 through 1.31.6; fixed in 1.30.6 and 1.31.7.
- **Source:** [NGINX security advisories](https://nginx.org/en/security_advisories.html)

### Finding 6 — NGINX TLS session-ticket forgery

- **Product:** NGINX
- **Issue:** CVE-2026-97629
- **Severity:** Medium (NGINX rating)
- **Description:** Automatic TLS session-ticket key rotation can permit a remote unauthenticated attacker to forge client TLS sessions under specific conditions.
- **Relevance:** Direct match to the monitored NGINX product.
- **Affected versions:** 1.23.2 through 1.31.6; fixed in 1.30.6 and 1.31.7.
- **Source:** [NGINX security advisories](https://nginx.org/en/security_advisories.html)

### Finding 7 — NGINX asynchronous-I/O use-after-free

- **Product:** NGINX
- **Issue:** CVE-2026-97205
- **Severity:** Medium (NGINX rating)
- **Description:** Use of asynchronous file I/O can trigger a use-after-free condition in affected NGINX releases.
- **Relevance:** Direct match to the monitored NGINX product.
- **Affected versions:** 0.8.11 through 1.31.6; fixed in 1.30.6 and 1.31.7.
- **Source:** [NGINX security advisories](https://nginx.org/en/security_advisories.html)

### Finding 8 — OpenSSH security update on Ubuntu

- **Product:** OpenSSH / Ubuntu
- **Issues:** CVE-2026-106552, CVE-2026-106553, CVE-2026-106555, CVE-2026-106582 through CVE-2026-106587
- **Severity:** Not stated in the Ubuntu notice
- **Description:** The update fixes nine issues including unintended SFTP file writes, GSSAPI credential exposure, command injection through crafted usernames, information disclosure, denial of service, and tunnel-restriction bypass.
- **Relevance:** Both OpenSSH and Ubuntu are directly monitored products.
- **Affected Ubuntu releases:** 22.04 LTS, 24.04 LTS, and 26.04 LTS.
- **Source:** [Ubuntu USN-8928-1](https://ubuntu.com/security/notices/USN-8928-1)

### Finding 9 — curl vulnerabilities in Ubuntu 26.04 LTS

- **Product:** Ubuntu 26.04 LTS `curl` package
- **Issues:** Sixteen CVEs, including CVE-2026-92392
- **Severity:** Mixed; Ubuntu does not give one advisory-wide severity, while curl rates CVE-2026-92392 High
- **Description:** The update addresses information disclosure, machine-in-the-middle risk, command injection, denial of service, local file overwrite, and potential code execution in curl/libcurl.
- **Relevance:** This is an official Ubuntu package advisory; applicability depends on whether the monitored Ubuntu systems run the affected package.
- **Sources:** [Ubuntu USN-8927-1](https://ubuntu.com/security/notices/USN-8927-1), [curl maintainer analysis of CVE-2026-92392](https://daniel.haxx.se/blog/2026/10/14/)

### Finding 10 — BIND vulnerabilities in Ubuntu

- **Product:** Ubuntu `bind9` package
- **Issues:** Twenty-four CVEs listed in USN-8929-1
- **Severity:** Not stated in the Ubuntu notice
- **Description:** The batch includes remotely triggerable denial-of-service conditions, DNS cache poisoning and DNSSEC validation bypasses, policy bypass, and unauthorized zone-content handling.
- **Relevance:** This is an official Ubuntu package advisory; applicability depends on whether BIND is installed. The notice covers Ubuntu 14.04 LTS through 26.04 LTS, with fixes for older releases requiring the applicable Ubuntu Pro or Legacy Support entitlement.
- **Source:** [Ubuntu USN-8929-1](https://ubuntu.com/security/notices/USN-8929-1)

### Possible match needing review

NGINX also released njs 1.0.2 for CVE-2026-101025 (malformed-XML memory exhaustion) and CVE-2026-101019 (inconsistent XML attribute values affecting signed-XML validation). njs is an official NGINX JavaScript module, but the product lists do not establish that it is deployed, and the source does not state severity. [NGINX release notice](https://nginx.org/)

### MongoDB ecosystem verification

The dedicated sweep checked MongoDB Server Community and Enterprise, `mongod`, `mongos`, Atlas and Atlas services, Ops Manager, Cloud Manager, Compass, `mongosh`, Database Tools, Kubernetes Operator, official drivers and connectors, BI Connector, Charts, Realm/App Services, and major official integrations and libraries. **No credible new MongoDB vulnerability was verified inside this run’s 24-hour window.** An October 14 Atlas Search availability incident was reviewed and excluded because it was not reported as a security vulnerability.

### Review priority

**Immediate review is recommended for CVE-2026-96951 because exploitation is confirmed.** Also prioritize exposed NGINX deployments and apply the applicable OpenSSH/Ubuntu updates. Confirm whether njs, curl, and BIND are installed before treating those conditional component findings as affected assets.
